source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-85: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 85 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume an authorized, isolated multi-node pilot with disposable copies, representative checkpoints, no production overwrite, and an unchanged CPU-staged fallback. Inventory GPU/storage/PCIe topology, NUMA and process/I/O affinity, filesystem and mount support, kernel, driver and runtime versions, container permissions, checkpoint format, durability semantics, request size, concurrency, queue depth, cache/compression, and contention. Test the falsifiable hypothesis that an evidenced active GDS path reduces end-to-end training I/O stall or host CPU versus a matched CPU-staged path at fixed workload without worsening p99 latency, errors, data integrity, or restartability. Measure storage throughput and GPU-DMA throughput separately in GB/s, plus end-to-end and stall time, host CPU%, GPU idle%, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, retries, errors, checksums, and interruption/node-loss recovery time with synchronized timestamps, units, repeated paired trials, cold/warm-cache and contention controls, and uncertainty. Change one factor at a time and require approval before rollout; quarantine outputs and revert to CPU staging on checksum mismatch, unrecoverable restart state, missing direct-path evidence, permission failures, or repeated threshold breaches.
